transcript:
Meeting start: 2025-09-12 16:00 UTC; Duration approx 52 minutes
Attendees: Alyssa Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Holt (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Rao (Kestrel CTO), Ethan Rivera (Head of Cloud Ops), Lisa Moreno (Legal), Samir Patel (ML Engineer)

Summary:
- POC scope for Kestrel Medical: validate Redwood inference for triage-assist model; focus on compliance (SOC2, ISO27001), SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, and on-prem / VPC readiness.
- Agree to run two benchmark passes (hosted vs private) using a 20k-turn sample and 95th percentile latency targets.
- Next steps: security pack, benchmark runbook, infra topology, schedule infra will-call.

Topics: POC success criteria; workload sizing and concurrency; benchmarks and metrics; security controls (SSO, RBAC, audit logging); deployment model options; timeline.

Auto-generated action items (captured above).

Transcript body:
00:00 Alyssa: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we appreciate you carving out time. I'm Alyssa, the AE. Marcus from our infra team will cover the technical requirements. Could we do quick intros?
00:12 Dr. Priya Rao: Hi, I'm Priya Rao, CTO at Kestrel Medical. We're leading this POC to see if we can offload our triage-assist model to a managed inference pipeline while keeping PHI controls in place.
00:22 Ethan Rivera: Ethan here, I run Cloud Ops; I'll be focused on network and KMS/HSM questions.
00:27 Lisa Moreno: Lisa from legal, I'll flag anything about data residency and retention.
00:31 Marcus Holt: Marcus, Redwood SE, will walk through benchmarks and the deployment options — hosted, dedicated, or private VPC.
00:38 Alyssa: Great. High level objectives: you told us offline you need a POC that proves latency under load, cost estimates, and security controls. Is that correct?
00:47 Dr. Priya Rao: Yep. Also we need to prove that audit logs capture all request/response metadata and that SAML SSO integrates with our Okta instance.
00:56 Alyssa: Perfect — that's in scope. Marcus, do you want to take the sizing section?
01:03 Marcus: Sure. Based on the notes Samir shared, the triage-assist model averages 150 tokens per call with a 1.2s median generation. For the POC we recommend two workload profiles: low parallelism burst (10 qps) for latency SLO verification, and sustained throughput (200 qps) for cost+scaling evaluation. For the benchmark we usually run a 20k-50k sample across both profiles.
01:30 Samir Patel: Quick note — our live traffic is spiky during mornings, we see short bursts of 70qps for 30s. We want to validate graceful degradation.
01:40 Marcus: Good to know. For bursts we use continuous batching with a per-tenant max batch size; we'll show the tradeoffs in the runbook. Our target 95th percentile latency for the triage model is under 800ms on dedicated, under 1.2s on hosted with cache warm.
01:57 Dr. Priya Rao: Are those numbers realistic for our safety thresholds? We need end-to-end under 1s ideally.
02:03 Marcus: E2E depends on network and pre/post-processing. For pure inference token gen, the numbers I quoted are server-side only. If you need strict E2E <1s we'll need a dedicated pool and aggressive batching config plus prefix KV cache for common prompts.
02:18 Ethan: On the network side, if we do private deployment we can reduce VPC egress. We also need to know what encryption-at-rest keys you expect us to use or if Redwood manages keys.
02:29 Alyssa: We support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and Dedicated via bring-your-own-key (BYOK) options. For hosted POC we can also integrate with your external KMS via an encrypted tunnel, but that's more setup.
02:41 Lisa: What's the SOC2 shape? We need evidence of controls, and ISO27001 is a hard ask for our compliance team.
02:48 Alyssa: Redwood is SOC2 Type II certified; we have ISO27001 in progress for certain services — Marcus can point to the control mappings in the pack. We will provide an executive summary, the SOC2 report under NDA, and a gap matrix against ISO if needed.
03:03 Marcus: I'll attach the compliance mapping doc — it shows control numbers, our logging retention, encryption standards, and what’s available in Private vs Hosted. Note: some ISO-specific artifacts are still being finalized, but the SOC2 attestation is current.
03:15 Lisa: Okay, we'll need to review the SOC2 and the list of subservice providers. Also retention of audit logs — do you store request/response bodies?
03:24 Marcus: By default we store metadata and request hashes. For hosted we do not retain full PII content beyond a configurable window; for Private deployments the customer can choose retention policy — logs can be shipped to your own SIEM. For the POC we can enable full debug capture behind NDA for benchmark runs.
03:39 Dr. Priya Rao: Good. For SSO we use Okta and SAML. We need role-based access tied to AD groups, and fine-grained RBAC so engineers can't access PHI unless authorized.
03:50 Marcus: We support SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning. RBAC maps to groups and you can restrict token scopes to teams. Audit events include user id, action, model, route, and request id.
04:03 Samir: Any gotchas with KV cache and model variants? We rely on per-patient context, so KV cache eviction must be explicit.
04:11 Marcus: We recommend session-scoped KV caching with TTLs you define. For PHI we suggest not caching personal identifiers; instead cache canonical prompts/behaviors and keep PII out of the cache. We can show config examples.
04:24 Ethan: About deployment modes — what's the friction to try dedicated vs on-prem? We are constrained by data residency in EU.
04:31 Alyssa: For EU residency we can do a private VPC in our EU region or an on-prem bundle. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and is faster to set up than fully air-gapped on-prem. Tradeoff: dedicated still has our control plane talking to your VPC for orchestration unless you choose the Private control plane option.
04:49 Lisa: If the control plane talks back, we need details on telemetry and minimum network egress. Also contractual guarantees for data access.
04:56 Marcus: We'll include a network diagram in the pack and min egress ports. For Private control plane we can remove outbound telemetry by request; it becomes a customer-managed control plane.
05:08 Dr. Priya Rao: Benchmarks — what's the methodology? We need reproducible runs that show tail latency, token-cost, throughput, and quality regression (hallucination rate).
05:18 Marcus: We propose two passes: 1) Functional correctness & quality run using 5k labeled examples to measure helpfulness, F1 on entity extraction, and hallucination checks. 2) Performance run using 20k queries to measure p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens per second, and cost. We'll provide the harness (scripted load generator) and metric dashboards.
05:37 Samir: For quality, we have a labeled set of 5k after de-identification; we'll share the format. We also want to test under encrypted payloads and confirm audit trails capture the de-id mapping.
05:47 Marcus: Great. For the quality tests we'll need ground truth labels; for hallucination measurement we'll define a scoring rubric. Expect two weeks to run both passes including tuning.
05:57 Alyssa: Timeline wise, if we get the dataset by 2025-09-18, Marcus can run benchmarks starting 09-20 and deliver a results deck by 09-26. Does that align with your internal timelines?
06:08 Ethan: That's tight but doable. We need to coordinate our infra window for the private run. Also, will you need service account access to our Okta for SSO setup?
06:17 Marcus: We typically request a test Okta SAML app with an engineer-level service user and SCIM rights for provisioning during POC. All actions are logged.
06:26 Lisa: Legal will want an NDA amendment to allow full debug logs containing de-identified PHI for the POC. We'll circle back.
06:33 Alyssa: Understood, Lisa. We'll add that as an action item.
06:36 Dr. Priya Rao: Two more items: 1) Can we simulate failure modes — e.g., model fallback to smaller variant if capacity is exhausted? 2) Can you show RBAC separation between engineering and clinical teams?
06:46 Marcus: Yes on both. We can demo automatic fallback policies and a role matrix that enforces least privilege. We'll include sample canary rollout and A/B config.
06:57 Samir: About metrics, can you export to our Prometheus/Grafana stack?
07:02 Marcus: Telemetry supports Prom remote write and can push to your SIEM. For POC we'll provide a Grafana dashboard with raw metrics and traces.
07:10 Alyssa: Quick recap of commitments: we'll send the SOC2 pack and compliance slides, Marcus will produce the benchmark runbook and run plan, and Kestrel will supply the dataset and infra details.
07:20 Lisa: Expect legal to email constraints; we'll try to get the NDA toggle by next week.
07:24 Ethan: I'll share VPC topology and our KMS vendor details (we use AWS KMS with external HSM for keys).
07:29 Alyssa: Noted. Any other risks?
07:32 Dr. Priya Rao: Concerned about cost visibility — we need token-level cost breakdown during the POC.
07:38 Marcus: We have token breakdowns per request and can annotate runs with cost analytics. We'll include that in the deliverables.
07:45 Samir: Minor transcription note — sometimes the transcript tool swaps Redwood product names; just flagging for the note.
07:50 Alyssa: Good catch. Last thing — would Kestrel prefer Redwood run the private POC in EU or try hosted first?
07:57 Dr. Priya Rao: Let's try hosted in EU region first to validate functionality, then run dedicated or private if latency or compliance needs force it.
08:07 Alyssa: That sounds sensible. We'll propose a schedule with two phases.
08:12 Marcus: I'll follow up with the runbook and a default benchmark config: 20k queries, 2 profiles (burst 10qps, sustained 200qps), measurement windows of 30m each, and quality suite of 5k labeled examples.
08:25 Alyssa: Thanks everyone — we'll send the security pack and proposed schedule. Any final questions?
08:31 Lisa: No, thanks.
08:33 Ethan: Nothing else.
08:34 Dr. Priya Rao: Thanks, bye.
08:35 Meeting end.
